mode: User-requested game-focused cleanup: remove wall branding and reduce foreground/background decoration
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit image 1 to apply the user's correction: "Let's not have the GitHub logo on the back wall; make the backdrop and foreground less decorative. This is for a game."

KEEP THE SUCCESSFUL PLAYER INTERFACE EXACTLY:
Preserve the layout and readability of the seven Tower portraits on the left, the large orange Developer and plinth in the center, the visual stats panel on the right, and the seven animation buttons along the bottom. Preserve every existing useful label, current selection and control size. Keep the model identity and pose. This is a focused cleanup and game-art simplification, not a new layout.
Image 2 is the actual game style authority: simple flat matte colors, low-poly assets and clear silhouettes.

REMOVE BRANDING:
Completely remove the large GitHub text AND Octocat mark from the back wall. Do not replace them with another corporate logo, mural, text or large emblem.
Remove GitHub/Octocat marks anywhere else in the scenery too, including the mug and distant building. Keep only the existing COPILOT / Copilot Hub game identity in the small top-left HUD. No other GitHub name, Octocat silhouette or decorative logo should remain anywhere.

SIMPLIFY THE BACKDROP:
Remove the entire green/cream contribution-square wall installation. Replace it and the old logo area with one calm, mostly plain matte blue-gray/ink wall plane, so the white Developer title remains readable.
Remove the branching pendant lights, coffee setup, shelves of books, visible sticky-note board, Review lettering and dense overlapping room furniture. Replace the complicated glass review-room framing on the left with simple quiet ivory/blue-gray wall geometry. Retain only a few large architectural planes and a broad window at upper right so the place still reads as a Hub interior.
Through the window show just a simplified section of campus path, two or three small faceted teal trees and soft sky/digital space. No large exterior buildings or logos, no busy distant offices. Keep these small and low contrast.
One understated simple bench far in the background is acceptable, but do not add decor to fill the cleared space. Empty visual space is intentional.
Keep the office reference only in the warm desk surface, ivory slabs, navy/blue-gray framing and soft daylight. This is a game screen with an understated room setting.

SIMPLIFY THE FOREGROUND:
Remove ALL foreground plants and planters, the GitHub mug, the closed notebook, the bottom cropped chair and the desk's other decorative props. They must not obscure or crowd the controls.
Keep a broad clean pale-oak desk plane below and between the interactive elements, with the near desk edge visible. Simplify wood to a flat warm color with almost no grain. No photographic material textures.
Do not add flowers, papers, mugs, cables, small widgets or new props.

MATCH THE GAME'S RENDERING:
Make the room and furniture closer to the actual low-poly game in image 2: simple geometry, matte solid colors, understated planar bevels and modest contact shadows. No realistic interiors photograph, microtexture, glossy lighting, decorative bokeh, dramatic depth of field or neon-heavy effects.
Retain depth in the controls, their dark neutral surfaces, pale-indigo selection, teal plinth edge and the character's canonical faceted geometry. The UI and model should be the clearest, highest-contrast things in the image.

FUNCTIONAL INVARIANTS:
Seven portraits and names: Base, Developer, Tester, Analyst, Security, Architect, Linter. Developer selected; no invented lock badges.
Developer title and "Direct-output specialist".
Stats labels Damage, Work, Action speed, Range, Compute with visual segmented gauges ONLY. No numbers, units, percentages, costs or totals.
Exactly seven animation choices: Rest, Idle, Work, Move, Place, Hit, Resolve. Idle selected. Absolutely no playback speed control, transport controls, timeline, scrubber, loop toggle or extra blank key.
Keep the model orbit arrows, camera Reset, "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom", and Back to Hub.
Preserve landscape 16:9 composition. Deliver one finished clean player-facing game screen. It should feel spacious, readable and ready to browse Towers, with the background serving the interface.
